lxc_6b70918b9a8ef726.text: GDP per hour compares a country’s economic output with its working hours.

lxc_21cae034eed581f7.text: Ireland, Norway, and Luxembourg rank very highly, but each country’s result has a different economic story.

lxc_e730175bdbb75f9a.text: Labour productivity compares economic output with the hours people work.

lxc_6aa14822d355ad08.text: A common measure is GDP per hour worked.

lxc_d59d4186fffb1115.text: GDP means the total value produced in an economy.

lxc_6fd270316dc4b15f.text: Imagine that a bakery produces goods worth 800 dollars during 10 hours of work.

lxc_270ced46e6b68b75.text: Its output is 80 dollars per hour.

lxc_984ff943d909270e.text: However, this measure is not simply a score for personal effort.

lxc_45cf542bf9f22964.text: Workers may produce more because they use better machines, faster technology, or a more effective system.

lxc_9d18e2f82aea5039.text: Investment and workplace organisation also matter.

lxc_a29bb9491de16d82.text: A person using modern equipment may produce more than an equally hardworking person using old equipment.

lxc_55689acca4942428.text: Therefore, high GDP per hour does not automatically mean that people are working harder.

lxc_ee77a428b92222be.text: To compare countries fairly, researchers use purchasing power parities.

lxc_39852066f76926de.text: These adjust for differences in prices between countries.

lxc_55f654b3648b44d5.text: Without this adjustment, the same amount of money could represent very different quantities of goods and services.

lxc_d23011072ef02720.text: In the comparison used here, Ireland ranks first for GDP per hour.

lxc_c2e6da249a3b1ebf.text: Norway and Luxembourg are also among the top three.

lxc_9a4fa5d0acebec9d.text: In 2023, the average across OECD countries was around 70 US dollars of GDP per hour.

lxc_6d567dcf9e427622.text: The strongest economies produced nearly twice that average.

lxc_97f7f9b31c34d83e.text: This large gap is interesting, but the ranking needs careful interpretation.

lxc_0f5c669f432ec875.text: A country’s industrial structure can strongly affect its result.

lxc_96db9932a1b2740d.text: The number does not tell us everything about ordinary workers, wages, or daily living conditions.

lxc_9b909a3f1df72d03.text: Ireland is home to many foreign-owned multinational enterprises, especially in technology and pharmaceuticals.

lxc_64d3693597920e60.text: These companies can report very large profits and valuable intellectual property in Ireland.

lxc_39e238f481c86739.text: Aircraft leasing also adds to measured economic activity.

lxc_be36c56ac42650d3.text: Together, these global activities can make Irish GDP extremely large.

lxc_929c0087b2230c10.text: However, much of this value may have a limited connection with local jobs and production.

lxc_580544c54f9a6cc0.text: If GDP is very high while the number of working hours is relatively small, GDP per hour becomes very high too.

lxc_cbe0af5035bf826c.text: This helps explain Ireland’s first-place position.

lxc_b312bd2fd9b17e16.text: It does not mean that every employee in Ireland produces more through personal skill or effort than every employee elsewhere.

lxc_89d64f748d67d841.text: The result partly reflects how multinational business activity appears in Ireland’s national accounts.

lxc_5560378751cdc804.text: Ireland, Norway, and Luxembourg all have high GDP per hour, but their economies are not identical.

lxc_70afa1eab541395a.text: Ireland’s figure is strongly affected by multinational technology and pharmaceutical companies.

lxc_a8e414a9db0abc96.text: Norway has a large energy sector, which creates high-value output.

lxc_9b4cded416affdc5.text: Luxembourg has a major finance sector as well as substantial multinational activity.

lxc_b55d2f91f4c4d3bd.text: The same ranking can therefore hide different sources of productivity.

lxc_c53151001e8fc477.text: Ireland’s result is closely connected to global company accounts.

lxc_b76ae9fc24720221.text: Norway’s energy resources are important, while Luxembourg’s financial services and multinational businesses play a major role.

lxc_6ba2ce4478a4c315.text: GDP per hour gives us a useful starting point, but it does not explain these differences by itself.

lxc_d6ab28be5a1dbf1c.text: We need to ask what kind of activity produces the measured value in each country.

lxc_e638a77a2f926974.text: A careful reader should examine more than one measure.

lxc_dee38562fd52989f.text: GNI per hour can be useful when multinational enterprises have a large effect on GDP.

lxc_0a548af40aaa7ee6.text: Ireland also uses modified Gross National Income, written GNI star or GNI*.

lxc_743bf829f5cf2b2e.text: It removes important globalisation effects to show a picture closer to the domestic economy.

lxc_937ac479da47175f.text: Modified GNI excludes effects connected with areas such as foreign-owned intellectual property and aircraft leasing.

lxc_2fb2b2b03055d2b8.text: It is closer to income linked with workers’ pay, Irish-owned businesses, and taxes received by the government.

lxc_df2ebbac74d6ab18.text: Official results for 2025 showed that Ireland’s modified GNI was much smaller than its GDP.

lxc_15b2eadd9609ec09.text: This does not make GDP per hour useless.

lxc_711e636212e7b95d.text: Instead, it shows why several measures are needed to understand productivity and local economic life.
